title: PAFO: Pareto Fairness Optimization for Personalized Reward Modeling

bias_targets.methodology: The paper measures 'personalization unfairness' by evaluating systematic disparities in reward prediction accuracy between users based on their 'preference support rate' (how common their preferences are in the population). It utilizes metrics such as the Coefficient of Variation (CV), Gini coefficient (GINI), and the slope of accuracy versus support rate on the Personal-LLM and DSP benchmarks.

Evaluated using the DSP dataset, which segments users into different stylistic preference groups (literature, entertainment, normal, business, academy). The paper compares the reward modeling accuracy for minority-represented styles (e.g., literature) versus majority-represented styles (e.g., academy).
